title: Relational Learning as World Modeling
abstract: arXiv:2610.16763v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Relational learning typically predicts from a database state, but decision making asks a different question: how will that state change under an action? In operational systems, the answer depends on system-specific dynamics that may not be visible in the database itself. We view each such system as a relational "world" and ask whether a model can infer how it behaves from observed executions. We introduce TabWM (Tabular World Model) and WorldRel, a generator of executable relational worlds for pretraining. Given executions from an unseen world, TabWM uses them as context to predict the sparse structured edits caused by a new action without parameter updates. Across 512 held-out worlds, complete-edit F1 rises from 0.016 with no observed executions to 0.685 with 64, where a correct edit must match its operation, relational location, and value. translated_title: 将关系学习视为世界建模
translated_abstract: 关系学习通常是从数据库状态出发进行预测，但决策制定提出了一个不同的问题：在某个动作的作用下，该状态将如何变化？在运营系统中，答案取决于系统特定的动态特性，而这些动态特性可能在数据库本身中并不可见。我们将每个这样的系统视为一个关系“世界”，并探究模型能否从观察到的执行过程中推断出它的行为方式。我们提出了TabWM（表格世界模型）和WorldRel——一个用于预训练的可执行关系世界生成器。给定来自某个未见过的世界的执行记录，TabWM将其作为上下文，在无需参数更新的情况下预测新动作所引起的稀疏结构化编辑。在512个留出世界上，完整编辑的F1分数从没有观察执行记录时的0.016提升到有64条执行记录时的0.685，其中正确的编辑必须同时匹配其操作、关系位置和值。由于这些预测是显式的关系编辑，它们可以被递归地应用以进行想象推演……
tldr: 该论文提出TabWM（表格世界模型）与WorldRel（可执行关系世界生成器），使模型能够通过观察执行记录推断关系世界的动态规律，在无需参数更新的情况下预测动作引发的数据库稀疏结构化编辑，在512个留出世界上将完整编辑F1从0.016提升至0.685。
en_tdlr: TabWM, a tabular world model pretrained on WorldRel-generated executable relational worlds, infers the dynamics of unseen systems from observed executions and predicts the sparse structured database edits caused by an action without parameter updates, raising complete-edit F1 from 0.016 to 0.685 across 512 held-out worlds.
